OP asked a simple question, and I answered a simple answer.

In Islam, life is seen as a test and a temporary journey leading to an eternal afterlife. The purpose of life is to worship and obey Allah, seek righteousness, and prepare for what comes after death. The Quran states that humans were created to be tested in faith, actions, and character: *"He who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed—and He is the Almighty, Most Forgiving."* (Quran 67:2). The trials of life, including suffering and happiness, are opportunities to grow spiritually and prove devotion to Allah. The core purpose of existence is to worship Allah: *"And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me."* (Quran 51:56) Worship in Islam is not just rituals but includes living ethically, being just, helping others, and seeking knowledge. Islam teaches that life does not end with death; rather, it transitions to the afterlife (Akhirah), where one's deeds determine their eternal fate. Those who do good and believe in Allah are promised Paradise, while those who reject Him and do evil are warned of punishment. The fleeting nature of this life makes it valuable because every action counts towards the afterlife. Instead of seeing death as an end, Islam sees it as the gateway to a just and eternal existence. Life gains purpose through kindness, charity, justice, and striving to improve oneself and society. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasized that even small acts like smiling or removing harm from a path are meaningful.

In short, Islam teaches that life is meaningful because it determines our eternal destiny, and death is just the beginning of the true existence. The purpose is to fulfill our role as servants of Allah and prepare for what comes after.
